lawyer: Md Noor Hossai AKM Fazlul Haque, Advocate -----For the Anti- Corruption Commission. (Respondent No. 2).
parties:
Mohoshin Miah (Md) ------ Convict-Appellant
Vs.
State and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
This criminal appeal, at the instance of the convict appellant under section 10 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 has been directed against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 4-3-2010 passed by the Special Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Special Case No.2 of 2009 arising out of Fatulla Police Station Case No. 20(4)/2007 convicting the appellant Md Mohoshin Mia under section 161 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act (Act No. Il of 1947) sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3(three) years with a fine of Taka 2,000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6 months more.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of the appeal, in short, is that Md Benzir Ahmed, Deputy Director of the Durniti Daman Commission (in short, the DUDAC), Narayanganj lodged the First Information Report (in short, the FIR) naming the present appellant as the sole accused alleging inter-alia, that accused Md Mohoshin Mia has been serving as Assistant Land Officer at Kashipur Union Land Office under Fatulla Police Station, district Narayanganj. One Abdus Salam alias Khokon from Kashipur village of Fatulla Police Station had approached the accused two months ago for mutation of his name pursuant to a deed of exchange being No. 6236 dated 24-12- 2003 by which he got 0.03 acres of land of RS plot No. 3116 corresponding to SA plot No. 1539 of khatian No. 3759 of mouza Kashipur but the accused had demanded Taka 5,000 to him as bribe. Abdus Salam Khokon expressed his inability to fulfill the demand of the accused to which the accused informed him that without the said amount his name will not be mutated for the said land but at one stage for the request of Abdus Salam Khokon he reducing the amount demanded Taka 4,000 with an advance of Taka 2,000. On completion of the said negotiation Abdus Salam Khokon gave Taka 2,000 with the required papers, when the accused asked him to meet after 15 days. Almost after 20 days when he had met with the accused, the accused informed him that for various reasons he is to pay more Taka 2,000 for the work.

3. Under the above circumstances Abdus Salam Khokon making a written complaint narrating the above facts to the District Officer, DUDAC, Narayanganj wanted to nab the accused at. the time of transaction of the said bribe and accordingly the allegation was registered as FIR No.3 of 2007 dated 10-4-2007 and making an inventory list of the Taka 4,000 presented by Abdus Salam Khokon was given back to him for handing over the same to the accused and ultimately the informant forming a trap party was awaiting in a nearby place of Kashipur Union Land Office and after getting signal he had entered into the office room of the accused along with Magistrate Mr Md Kamruzzaman and caught the accused read handed with Taka 4,000 received from Abdus Salam Khokon, The accused on their query admitted before the informant and the Magistrate that he had received Taka 4,000 from Abdus Salam Khokon as bribe. They found the similarity between the recovered money with the inventory list prepared on the same day. The informant arrested the accused and seized the 8 (eight) notes of Taka 500 under a seizure list along with a DCR book and narrating the above facts lodged the FIR with Fatulla Police Station, Narayanganj.

4. On the basis of the said FIR, Fatulla Police Station Case No. 20.dated 10-4-2007 corresponding to GR No. 232 of 2007 were started. The case was investigated by PW 12 Md Helaluddin Sharif, who on completion of the investigation submitted report recommending the trial of the accused under section 161 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and the case was ultimately transmitted in the Court of Sessions Judge and Senior Special Judge, Narayanganj where the case was registered as Special Case No: 6 of 2008 and the cognizance was also taken by the Senior Special Judge, Narayanganj.

5. On 14-7-2008 charge under section 161 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 was framed against the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The case was tried by the Senior Special Judge, Narayanganj till 28-1-2009 and within this span of time 5(five) witnesses were examined by that Court. Thereafter, the case was transferred in- the Court of Special Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka where the case was renumbered as Special Case No.2 of 2009. The remaining witnesses were examined by the Special Judge, Court No.4, Dhaka and after examination of 13 witnesses in all the accused was examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure when he repeated his innocence and declined to examine any defence witness but submitted some papers which have been kept in the record.

6. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence and other materials on record found the accused guilty under section 161 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and sentenced him as aforesaid. The convict appellant being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment of the trial Court preferred this appeal in this Court.

7. Mr Md Noor Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant supporting of the appeal and assailing the judgment of the trial Court submits that the informant who led the trap party in nabbing the accused during the alleged transaction of bribe had proceeded illegally without compliance of the provisions of law. He did not obtain any sanction for trapping the case from the lawful authority. As such, the whole act of trap has become illegal and on the basis of the said illegal trap there cannot be any legal case against the convict appellant.

8. The learned Advocate next submits that the total prosecution case is based on some wrong notion. The accused at the relevant time has been serving at Kashipur Union Land Office as Vhumi Sahakari Karmakarta, commonly known in the revenue sector as Tahshilder. The accused was approached for some illegal works by Abdus Salam Khokon and since the accused did not pay heed to the said request, he (Abdus Salam Khokon) creating a plot of trap with the help of the informant had filed the present case. The trial Court did not at all consider that at the time of occurrence, the accused repeatedly told to the persons present there that the money given by Abdus Salam Khokon was a part payment of the rents of their ancestral property and the said facts had been admitted by most of the important witnesses including the Magistrate himself. But the trial Court without considering the said important evidence found the accused guilty under those sections of law.

9. He also submits that the trial Court failed to consider that the said Abdus Salam Khokon is a neighbour of the Kashipur Union Land Office who had easy access and approach in the said land office. Since the accused was not complying with the illegal request of Abdus Salam Khokon he arranged the trap case in order to cause harm to the accused with the help of the informant.

10. The learned Advocate further submits that the accused being an Assistant Land Officer has been serving in his office with the reputation but the shrewd and cunning Abdus Salam Khokon very tactfully in the name of making part payment of the revenue for their common ancestral property created this case but the accused being a man of simple minded could not understand the tricks of Abdus Salam Khokon as a result he has become the victim of circumstances and the trial Court had totally failed to appreciate their defence case. The trial Court should have considered that the prosecution could not prove the charge relying on any nitid and cogent evidence. Thus, the judgment and the order of conviction and sentence awarded upon the convict appellant are liable to be set aside acquitting him from the charge labelled against him.

11. On the other hand, Mr AKM Fazlul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 opposing the appeal and supporting the judgment of the trial Court submits that the accused from the very beginning of the case has been trying to misdirect the prosecution case in order to non-track the prosecution case. He categorically submits that the 8 notes of Bangladeshi Taka 500 was found in the possession of the accused which he had taken as bribe from Abdus Salam Khokon as part of his stipulation that he will do the needful to mutate the name of Abdus Salam Khokon pursuant to a deed of exchange being No. 6236 but the accused very cunningly has introduced a defence case that accused had taken the said amount from Abdus Salam Khokon as part payment of the revenue of their common ancestral property but Abdus Salam Khokon had never approached the accused for taking any revenue for their common ancestral property. Abdus Salam Khokon was never entrusted by his family members for making payment of the revenue of their common ancestral property. The transaction in question had taken place for mutating the name of Abdus Salam Khokon for the specific 0.03 acres of land and before handing over the said Taka 4,000 to the accused an inventory list was prepared for the said amount at DUDAC office, Narayanganj. The informant who led the trap party had obtained permission from his authority following to the respective Rules and in a case like this obtaining of permission for trap is a official procedure and that is always concerned between the authority and the officer who will led a trap party and the same cannot be visible to others and for a successful trap the leader of the trap party will give importance so that the information of the trap case cannot be leaked out and if for any reason the information of trap case is leaked out the whole purpose and scheme of the trap will be frustrated. So, the concerned officer will take cautious measure in taking the permission, so that the purpose of the trap cannot be vanished at the very initial stage of the occurrence.

12. He also submits that if for the sake of argument it is conceded for a moment that the per- mission was not obtained by the leader of the trap party that is not at all fatal in a case like this and the same is curable under section 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Moreso, the record will go to show that there is no case in the luggage of the defence that the informant in order to serve his any illegal interest had led the trap party and there is no case in the hands of the defence that the relation between the leader of the trap party and the accused was inimical before the occurrence of this case. So, the bonafide act of the leader of the trap party in order to discharge his official duty cannot be called in question to save the accused from the grip of the case.

13. He next submits that it is fact that the accused at the time of arrest tried to establish that he had taken those Taka 4,000 from Abdus Salam Khokon as part of the payment of the revenue of his ancestral property but that is not fact at all and the trial Court rightly disbelieved the said very cunning and shrewd defence case of the accused. On the date of occurrence the accused taking Taka 4,000 handed over the DCR connected to the mutation of the name of Abdus Salam Khokon and the said handing over of the papers regarding the mutation of name of Abdus Salam Khokon undoubtedly leads to believe that Abdus Salam Khokon had gone to the Kashipur land office, to hand over the bribe money. The trial Court on a proper scanning and consideration of the evidence and other materials on record rightly found the accused guilty under section 161 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. So, the judgment of the trial Court did not call for any interference from this Court. As such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

14. I have considered the above submissions and the arguments of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record particularly the exhibited documents, the documents filed by the defence at the time of examination under section 342 of the Code, the judgment of the trial Court and other connected materials available in the record.

15. In order to appreciate the arguments as advanced by the learned Advocates of both the parties let us have a look into the evidence on the record.

16. PW 1 Benzir Ahmed, the Deputy Director of DUDAC, testified that on 10-4-2007 he was posted at Narayanganj on that date Abdus Salam Khokon having been in his office filed a written complaint stating inter-alia that two months ago he had approached accused Md Mohshin Mia for mutating his name, when the accused demanded Taka 5,000 to him and after a bargaining the amount was fixed as Taka 4,000 and after one week he gave Taka 2,000 and the papers to the accused when he (Abdus Salam Khokon)was asked to meet with him after two weeks and accordingly Abdus Salam Khokon had met with the accused after 20 days and on that date accused reshuffling the amount demanded more Taka 4,000 to him. He further stated that Abdus Salam Khokon narrating the above facts in his petition of complaint requested him to nab the accused red handed at the time of transaction of the bribe and accordingly the allegation was registered as GR No. 3/7 dated 10-4-2007, he preparing an inventory list of Taka 4,000 which was intended to be used for giving bribe to the accused again delivered the same to Abdus Salam Khokon and at 14.30 hours he was awaiting in a nearby place of the Kashipur land office along with Magistrate Mr Kamruzzaman and the members of Rapid Action Battalion (in short, the RAB) and at 15-00 hours he having got the signal from Abdus Salam Khokon had entered into the office of the accused who on their interrogation admitted that he had taken Taka 4,000 as bribe and he brought out Taka 4,000 from the left sided pocket of his trouser and they found similarity between the inventory list and the said recovered money. They arrested the accused and seized the said money along with the wearing pant of the accused, a DCR book and a rent receipts book in presence of the witnesses and thereafter he narrating the above facts lodged the FIR with the Fatulla Police Station under section 161 of the Penal Code and 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. He proved the FIR and his signature in it, marked exhibits 1 and 1/1, the seizure list and his signature, marked exhibits 2 and 2/1, the petition of complaint filed by Abdus Salam Khokon, exhibit 3; the inventory list, exhibit 4 and the requisition for the Magistrate exhibit 5. He also identified the 8 notes of Taka 500 recovered from the accused, marked as material exhibits 1-VIII, the DCR and the rent receipts book, marked as material exhibits IX and X, the wearing pant of the accused, marked as material exhibit XII. He identified the accused in the Court.

17. In cross-examination of the defence he stated that Abdus Salam Khokon had come in his office on 10-4-2007 at 10-00 am and he stayed there for two hours, he cannot say where Abdus Salam Khokon had filed the petition for mutating his name. He did not examine the Assistant Commissioner (Land) before taking the action on the subject, a DCR was issued in the name of Abdus Salam Khokon on 29-3-2007 and he cannot say whether he (Abdus Salam Khokon) had got the mutation parch a on 29-3-2007 or not. He cannot say whether Abdus Salam Khokon had gone to the Tahshil office for making payment of the rent of his uncle. He denied the defence suggestion that the money which was recovered from the accused was the part payment of the rent belonged to the ancestral property of Abdus Salam Khokon. He further stated that Abdus Salam Khokon made the signal through gesture. He denied the defence suggestion that since the mutation was completed before 10-4-2007, so the transaction of bribe on that date is immaterial.

18. PW 2 Md Emran AIi, Inspector of Police testified that on 10-4-2007 he was posted as Officer-in-Charge at Fatulla Police Station and on that date at 20.45 hours he recorded the present case on the basis of the FIR lodged by Benzir Ahmed, Deputy Director of DUDAC. He proved the FIR column and his signature in it, marked Exhibits 6 and 6/1. He also adds that the case was investigated by the DUDAC. There was no cross- examination of PW 2.

19. PW 3 Abdus Salam alias Khokon at whose instance the case was initiated and started testified that in order to mutate his name for 0.03 acres of land of RS plot No. 3116 two months ago of the date of occurrence he had a dialogue with the accused when he demanded Taka 5,000 to him and after a short bargaining the amount was fixed as Taka 4,000 and after one week of the said contract he gave Taka 2,000 to the accused when he was asked to meet with him (accused) within 15 days along with the rest amount and almost after 20 days of the first transaction he met with the accused when he demanded more Taka 4,000 and since he was unwilling to make the payment of Taka 4,000 as bribe, he informed the occurrence to Benzir Ahmed, Deputy Director, DUDAC who took a written allegation from him, he proved his signature on the said written allegation, marked exhibit 3/1, the Deputy Director sent a requisition to the Deputy Commissioner, Narayanganj for a Magistrate and they made a inventory list of Taka 4,000 comprising 8 notes of Taka 500 each and handed over the same to him for giving to the accused, both he and the trap party under the leadership of Deputy Director, DUDAC had gone in the land office, he gave Taka 4,000 to the accused whereupon the members of the RAB coming to the land office caught the accused red handed with the said Taka 4,000 and found the similarity between the recovered notes and the inventory list.

20.He also stated that when he gave Taka 4,000 to the accused he was given 3 papers of mutation and at that time the members of the trap party had arrested the accused red handed. The rent receipt bears the date of 10-4-2007.

21. In cross-examination of the defence he stated that on 10-4-2007 he had gone in the land office, the accused told him that he will do the needful for mutating his name and he cannot say whether he had filed any petition for mutating his name or not, on the date of occurrence the accused had handed over the papers of the mutation to him at 3.00 pm. The accused gave him the porch a of mutation. He denied the defence suggestion that he got the mutation porcha on 6-3-2007 and DCR on 29-3-2007.

22. He denied the suggestion that the accused did not give any DCR on 10-4-2007. The land of plot No. 1664 is their ejmali property. He further denied the defence suggestion that the mutation was completed on 6-3-2007.

23. He further stated that on handing over the money to the accused he got the 3 papers from the accused, Mofizuddin is his uncle, the land of CS plot No. 1664 is their ejmali property, he denied the defence suggestion that he unsuccessfully requested the accused for exoneration of revenue of Taka 7,132 of the said ejmali land. He denied the further defence suggestion that he being annoyed of the said refusal created the present case with the help of the RAB. He denied the further defence suggestion that on the date of occurrence he made a part payment of Taka 4,000 out of the amount of Taka 7,132 requesting him to issue receipts with the assurance that the rest of money will be paid soon and in the name of bringing of the rest money he brought the RAB. He further denied the defence suggestion that he tried to misappropriate their ejmali property with the help of the accused and since the accused did not help him he had created the present case against the accused.

24. PW 4 Md Abdul Khaleq testified that on 10-4-2007 he was posted as Sanchay Bureau Officer at Narayangan, the Deputy Director of OUOAC, Narayanganj in his presence made a inventory list of 8 notes of Taka 500, he proved his signature on the said inventory list, marked exhibit 4/2. In cross-examination of the defence he stated that he put his signature at 2.30 pm of the day.

25. PW 5 Khondker Shamsul Alam testified that on 10-4-2007 he was posted at Narayanganj Sports Office, on that day Benzir Ahmed, an Officer of DUDAC made the inventory list of 8 notes of Bangladeshi Taka 500 in his presence, he proved his signature on the list, marked Exhibit No. 4/3. In cross-examination of the defence, he stated that he cannot say as to why the inventory list was prepared.

26. PW 6 Md Serajul Haque testified that on 10-4-2007 at 2-45pm the occurrence of this case took place at Kashipur Union Land Office and in his presence Taka 4,000 was recovered from the accused and the same was seized under a seizure list. He proved his signature on the seizure list, marked exhibit 2/2. In cross-examination of the defence he stated that he knows the complainant, he did not find the complainant to hand over taka to the accused, the accused was telling the gathering that the complainant gave the Taka to him as part payment of the rent.

27.PW 7 Md Anisur Rahman testified that on the date of occurrence he had gone to Kashipur Tahshil office at 2-00/3-00 pm of the day, he found a person to give Taka 4,000 to the accused, the government official slapped the accused and recovered Taka 4,000 from him under a seizure list and he put his signature on the seizure list, marked exhibit 2/3. In cross-examination of the defence he stated that Abdus Salam Khokon gave Taka 4,000 to the accused, the accused was demanding more money on which the complainant asked the accused to issue receipt and within short time he will manage the rest money. The accused was telling the gathering that he received rents.

28. PW 8 Tanjina Islam testified that Vaskor Roaza was posted as Kanungo in the office of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) at Narayanganj Sadar who died later on. The file of the mutation case No. 6154/06-07, the khatian books comprising khatian No. 5388, rent receipts of mutation and the certified copy of the mutation khatian in all 16 pages was in the custody of Vaskor Roaza and since he is no more in the world she (PW 8) produced the same in the Court, marked material Exhibit No. XI series. She adds that on 20-2-2008, the file of the mutation case was seized. These papers were under his (Vaskor Roaza) custody and after his death the same were found in the almira. On 20-2-2008 the Investigating Officer seized the mutation case Nos. 6154/06-07 under a seizure list which was witnessed by Kanungo Vaskor Roaza and the same was left behind in the zimma of Vaskor Roaza. She proved the seizure list and zimmanama. The signature of Vaskor Roaza on those papers has been marked as exhibits 7/1 and 8/1.

29. In cross-examination of the defence, she stated that on 10-4-2007 Taka 2 was received from Abdus Salam Khokon through the receipt No. 714652 dated 10-4-2007 for the land of SA plot No. 1539 corresponding to RS plot No. 3116 of Kashipurmouza for an area of 0.03 acres, marked Exhibit No. X(i). She further stated that on 17-7-2007 and 25-7-2007 through 2 rent receipts being receipt Nos. 201869 and 201897 for the land of SA plot No. 1664 of khat in No. 551 rents for the years from 1408 to 1414 BS were received in the name of Mofizuddin at a worth of Taka 3,566 on each occasion, on 17-7-2007 one Amirul Islam and on 25-7-2007. Abdus Salam Khokon paid the said rents on behalf of Mafiz Uddin. She also stated that she had joined in the post of Assistant Commissioner (Land) on 10-9-2008 and Vaskor Roaza died on 6-11-2008.

30. PW 9 Md Nahim Mia testified that he has been serving at Kashipur Union Land Office in the post of Sub-Assistant Officer of Land, on 20- 2-2008 the Investigation Officer, Helal Sharif seized the record of Mutation Case No. 6154/06-07 in his presence and the same was placed in the zimma of Kanungo Vaskor Roaza. He proved his signature on the seizure list and Jimmanama, marked Exhibit Nos. 7/2 and 8/2. In cross-examination of the defence he stated that the Investigating Officer did not examine him at any point oftime, he and the accused used to work sitting side by side in the same office and they have worked jointly for 10 months. He knows the main complainant who is a neighbor of their office who used to visit their office from time to time, there took place a hitch between the main complainant and the accused for the payment of rents of some land for 7 years. The seized Taka 4,000 is not connected with the mutation of the name of the main complainant. Normally they used to deposit the money in the Bank after one week of the collection. He further stated that the main complainant paid Taka 4,000 to the accused as part payment of Taka 7,132.

31. PW 10 Md Majibur Rahman testified that on 20-2~2008 at 12 noon an officer of the office of the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Narayanganj produced some papers before the Investigating Officer of this case and he put his signature on the seizure list, marked exhibits 7/3 and 8/3. In cross-examination of the defence he stated that he has been serving in the DUDAC for the last 25 years. The mutation case of the complainant was seized. He denied the defence suggestion that he has deposed falsely to favour the prosecution.

32. PW 11 Kamruzzman testified that he was posted as Assistant Commissioner from 2-7-2005 to 20-5-2008 at Narayanganj and at present he has been serving in the Collectorate of Mymensingh, on 10-4-2007 he on the verbal direction of Deputy Commissioner, Narayanganj had met with Benzir Ahmed, the Deputy Director of DUDAC and he had gone at KashipurTahsil Office with him where an elderly man informed the Captain of RAB that the Tahshilder had taken Taka 4,000 as bribe from him but the accused denied the allegations, they found Taka 4,000 in the pocket of the trouser of the accused. They also found the similarity between the recovered money and the inventory list and after the arrest of the accused there was a photo sessions of the recovery. The money was seized and Benzir Ahmed himself prepared the seizure list. He proved his signature on the seizure list, marked Exhibit 2/4. He identified the seized 8 notes of Taka 500 also, He further stated that the rent receipts bearing No. 714601 to 714700 and the DCR book Nos. 16837 were also seized in his presence. In cross-examination of the defence he stated that he put his signature on the seizure list. At the time of occurrence Captain of RAB and the officer of DUDAC were present with him. He personally found the recovery of the money from the accused. After the repeated hammering of the Captain of RAB and Benzir Ahmed accused himself brought out the money from his trouser and . there were more money save and except Taka 4,000 but he cannot say the exact figure. The accused was telling repeatedly that the recovered money was the part payment of an amount given by Abdus Salam Khokon but Abdus Salam Khokon did not admit the same

33. PW 12 Helaluddin Sharif, the Investigating Officer of this case testified that he was appointed as Investigating Officer of the case on 23-1-2008 and started his investigation on and from 30-1-2008. He visited the place of occurrence and recorded the statements of the witnesses. On 6-2-2007 the mutation case No. 6154/06-07 was started. The Assistant Commissioner (Land) asked accused Mohshin Mia to furnish his report on or before 28-2-2007 and the Assistant Commissioner . (Land) accepted the proposal of the mutation on 5-3-2007, on 6-3-2007 the mutation porcha was prepared by accused Mohsin and was counter signed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) and after a short gap on 29-3-2007 a DCR for Taka 28 was issued in favour of Abdus Salam Khokon but no rent receipt was issued. He found in his investigation that since there was a dialogue between the accused and Abdus Salam Khokon for unlawful gain of the accused, he (accused) intended to issue the rent receipt on 10- 4-2007 on completion of the transaction but before handing over Taka 4,000 as bribe Abdus Salam Khokon informed the occurrence to the DUDAC office Narayanganj and the accused receiving Taka 4,000 on 10-4-2007 handed over the rent receipt for Taka 2 being receipt No. 714652 dated 10-4-2007 and at that time the trap party nabbed the accused led by Benzir Ahmed, Deputy Director of DUDAC in presence of Magistrate Mr Kamruzzman and other members of the trap party. The said bribe money of Taka 4,000 was recovered from the left sided pocket of the trouser of the accused. He submitted the memo of evidence on 10-3-2008 and the DUDAC approved the filing of charge sheet on 16-6-2008, thereafter on 18-6-2008 he submitted the charge sheet in this case.

34. In cross-examination of the defence he stated that he cannot say as to when he had joined in the DUDAC, the FIR was lodged on 10-4-2007 when Benzir Ahmed was Deputy Director of DUDAC at Narayanganj, he received the record for investigation on 30-1-2008 and got the sanction on 16-6-2008, the sanction was given by Mr Habibur Rahman, one of the Commissioner of DUDAC, Abdus Salam Khokon had filed a petition for mutating his name which he found at the time of investigation, the accused issued the rent receipt of Taka 2 on 10-4-2007 on receiving the bribe money of Taka 4,000, he did not examine the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) and Upazila Nirbahi Officer, there is no dwelling hut adjacent to the place of occurrence, he did not know Abdus Salam Khokon personally, he did not know whether Abdus Salam Khokon had approached the accused for cancelling the mutation in the name of his cousin, he did not find anything that for the said matter the relationship between Abdus Salam Khokon and the accused was deteriorating, the accused did not disclose to him that on 10-4-2007 Abdus Salam Khokon had tried to make payment of the rents for 0.39 acres of land. He denied the defence suggestion that Abdus Salam Khokon paid Taka 4,000 out of total rents of 7,132, he also denied the defence suggestion that Abdus Salam Khokon putting the accused on leg had left the place of occurrence for the rest amount of Taka 3,132. He denied the defence suggestion that the recovered money is not the bribe money. He denied the further defence suggestion that the accused did not receive any bribe from Abdus Salam Khokon.

35. PW 13 and the last witness Md Amirul Islam testified that his father name is Hazi Aman Ullah who is still alive. Mofizuddin was his uncle who is dead now, on 17-7-2007 he paid the rents for the land of S.A plot No. 1664 of their share, the land is their paternal property, there is a partition deed between his father and uncle in respect of the said land, he paid the rents of his portion on 17-7-2007 and since the land stands in the name of Mofizuddin they are paying the rents in his name, Abdus Salam Khokon is his cousin. Abdus Salam Khokon has been living in the land which stands in the name of Mofizuddin but he paid the rents of their portion, Mofizuddin has 3 sons. Advocate Harul Kabir is one of the son. He further stated that he heard it that an occurrence of giving bribe was taken place on 10-4-2007 which arose out of a mutation case of Abdus Salam Khokon, he paid the rents after 3 months of the occurrence for the portion of his father.

36. In cross-examination of the defence he stated Mofizuddin had 3 sons but cannot say how many daughters he had. There is a partition deed among his father and uncle but he did not bring the same in the Court. He denied the defence suggestion that there is no any partition deed among the co-sharer rather Mofizuddin alone had been possessing the said land, he was not present in the place of occurrence on 10-4-2007, he has dwelling hut on the land of plot No. 1664 and in the said plot there are 81 decimals of land. He denied the defence suggestion that he has deposed falsely to serve the purpose of Abdus Salam Khokon.

37. These are the evidence that have been given by the prosecution in this case. From the evidence discussed above it appears that the prosecution examined 13 witnesses in all out of which PWs 4 and 5 are the witnesses of the inventory list of 8 Bangladeshi notes of Taka 500 which were used in giving the bribe to the accused. PWs 6,7 and 11 are the witnesses of the seizure list as in their presence the said 8 notes of Taka 500 along with some other papers were seized at Kashipur Union land office immediately after recovery of the bribe money from the accused. PW 2 is the recording Officer of the case. PW 12 is the Investigating Officer. PWs 9 and 10 are the seizure list witnesses of mutation file and some other documents. PW 13 was examined to prove the payment of rents for the land of plot No. 1664on 17-7-2007. PW 3 is Abdus Salam Khokon at whose instance the case was initiated and PW 1 is the informant of this case under whose leadership the trap party moved to the place of occurrence for nabbing the accused.

38. From the evidence led by the prosecution and the cross-examination thereof and the suggestion made on behalf of the defence to the prosecution witnesses it reveals to me that the receiving of Taka 4,000 by the accused from Abdus Salam Khokon and the recovery of the said Taka 4,000 on 10-4-2007 from the physical possession of the accused has not been denied by the accused rather the same fact has been admitted in this case adding some fact that the accused had received the said taka as part payment of the rents of the ancestral property of Abdus Salam Khokon. Thus the real controversy between the prosecution and the defence appears as to the purpose of giving of the said money to the accused.

39. The very plain and simple prosecution case is that pursuant to a dialogue taken place for mutating the name of Abdus Salam Khokon relying on a ewaz deed for 0.03 acres of land he (Abdus Salam Khokon) gave Taka 4,000 to the accused a-s bribe while the defence case is that Abdus Salam Khokon gave those Taka to him as part payment of the rents for the land of plot No. 1664 which is their ancestral property but Abdus Salam Khokon very cunningly and cleverly turned the said fact into a fact of giving bribe to the accused.

40. Thus, is my consideration the real controversy between the parties is whether the money was given or taken by the accused as bribe for mutating the name of Abdus Salam Khokon or he had taken the same as part payment of the rents for the land of plot No. 1664.

41. Apart from this controversy there are some other allegations on the part of defence regarding the initiation ofthe case and submission of the investigation report. It is the arguments of the appellant before me that in order to lay a trap to nab an accused at the time of commission of any offence in view of the Rule 16 of the Durniti Daman Commission Bidhimala, 2007 (in short, the Bidhimala) prior permission from the Commissioner-in-charge is mandatory but without any proper compliance of the said Rule 16 the trap was made. So, the trap as well as the filing of the case capitalizing the said trap is illegal.

42. The further arguments of the appellant is that without examining the accused in compliance of the Rules 8 and 11 of the Bidhimala filing of the case and submission of the Police report is also illegal. So, the very cognizance taken by the Court below on the basis of the said defective report is not also legal and fair which have ultimately vitiated the trial of the case as a whole.

43. Now, to address the grievances of the appellant as to the laying down of the trap on 10- 4-2007 it appears from the record that there is nothing in the record to show that any permission before the trap or even after the trap was ever taken from the commissioner-in-charge. From the evidence of PW 1 there is nothing in the record to show that permission was ever sought to the com- missioner in order to comply the Rule 16 of the Bidhimala.

44. In this respect the learned Advocate for the appellant referring the case of Md Rezau lKabi  vs the State, 14 MLR 482 submits that a trap without prior permission is always illegal. In the referred case it has been held by this Court that any trap without the prior permission of the commissioner-in-charge of the investigation is bad and illegal in the law. As such, if any proceeding is started on the basis of such type of trap that is the abuse of the process of the law.

45. But Mr AKM Fazlul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 submits that it is fact that in the reported case of 14 MLR 482 it has been held by this Court that before laying down any trap without any permission from the commissioner in charge of investigation pursuant to the Rue 16 has been held illegal but the operation of the said judgment has been stayed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh at the instance of the Anti-Corruption Commission and he in support of his such submission submitted the judgment passed by the Appellate Division dated 13-11-2012 in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 423 of 2009. Since the operation of the judgment of the reported case of 14 MLR 482 has been stayed by the Appellate Division, the said judgment deserves no consideration at this stage.

46. The learned Advocate for the respondent No.2 on the same subject referring the case of Nuruzzaman vs State reported in 14 BLC 51 submits that in the reported case on Mrs Rahima Akter, Assistant Teacher of a school at Fatikchari drew the attention of Directorate of Anti-Corruption Commission of Divisional Office, Chittagong that accused Md Nuruzzarnan of that case who has been serving as Upazila Education Officer, Fatikchari intended to take bribe from her and on the basis of the said information, the said officer of Anti-Corruption Commission, Chittagong made a trap and nabbed the accused Md Nuruzzaman successfully and a regular case was filed on the basis of the said fact and as against the cognizance of the said case a proceeding to quash the case under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was filed in this Court by the accused Md Nuruzzaman and in that case it was argued that the trap was led without the prior permission of the Commissioner-in-charge of investigation of Anti-Corruption Commission. In the said case it was argued on behalf of the Anti-Corruption Commission that permission as laid down in the Rule 16 does not mean always written permission rather there is every risk if the written permission is obtained before the operation in that case the occurrence and fact of the case will be leaked out, so then: will be no trap case at all and for many reason it is not viable for the field officer to take written or prior permission from the commissioner-in-charge. In that case after laying down of the trap, permission was obtained from the commission in charge of investigation of Anti-Corruption Commission, Dhaka. In answering the grievances of the accused Nuruzzaman this Court in the reported case of 14 BLC 51 made the following observation:

"In the instant case, the Director of the Commission, Mr Md Zulfiquer Ali Mazumder led the trap operation and it is stated in the counter- affidavit of opposite party No.2 that before undertaking such operation, he sought permission from Md Habibur Rahman, Commissioner (Investigation) to lead the operation and he was permitted to do so. Written permission is neither required under the Rule, nor it is practicable. It may be noted here that Mr Md Habibur Rahman is the concerned Commissioner for the purpose of according such permission who. used to sit in the Head Officer in Dhaka and it is not possible on the part of the Director staying at Chittagong to obtain written permission from the authority in writing in case of such urgent need." (para 6 of the judgment)

47. From the judgment of this Court delivered in the case of Md Nuruzzaman it appears that this Court opined that for a field officer staying at Chittagong it is not possible on his part to obtain written permission from the authority in writing. I find it difficult to show any disagreement with this valuable observation of this Court.

<u>48. But in the reported case, the permission was sought even verbally but the same is also absent in this case. The Bidhimala came into force on 291h March, 2007 whereas the trap in connection of this case was made on 10th April, 2007, that is, after 11 days of the promulgation of the Bidhimala the occurrence of this case was taken place. In that view of the matter, the permission either in written or oral was mandatory for the field officer for laying down a trap and in my consideration every law and Rule is enacted in a civilized society to obey it and to serve the best purpose of the people and not to violate it and if the law enforcing agency who have been entrusted with the duty to enforce the law and Rules of the country ignore the same, what is the necessity for the enactment of the law and the Rules. In that view of the matter, the PW 1 who led the trap party should have moved to the place of occurrence taking either verbal or written permission from his authority as laid down in the Rule 16 of the Bidhimala.</u>

49. In this connection the learned Advocate for the respondent No.2 submits that the provisions of seeking permission for trap has been enacted in the Rule so that there cannot be abusive use of the trap and that is an administrative measure required to be carried out by the field officer of the Anti-Corruption Commission but trap with permission or without any permission do not materially affect in the result of the trap case and there is no virtual effect on the action of the trap and if any trap is taken place without the prior per-mission of the authority that is not prejudicial to the accused and there is no defence case that PW 1 who led the trap party was influenced by Abdus Salam Khokon to lead the trap party for any other reason than that of the bringing into the light of the corruption of the accused in discharging his official duty, so if there is any defect in conducting the trap that is curable under section 537 ofthe Code of Criminal Procedure.

50. In my consideration there cannot be any excuse in obtaining the permission for trap following the provisions of Rule 16 of the Bidhimala but if for any reason a trap is conducted without the prior permission of the commissioner-in-charge what may be the consequence of the same

51. This type of case is tried by the Special Judge, appointed under the previsions of Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. Section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 provides that the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, so far as they are not in consistent with the Act will be applicable to the proceeding of the Court of a Special Judge. So, the provisions of Code of Criminal Procedure which is not inconsistent with the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 is also applicable in the trial of the cases by the Special Judge.

<u>52. As such, I am of the opinion that since there appears no special defence case on behalf of the accused in respect of the trap case that the PW 1 who led the trap party had any connivance with Abdus Salam Khokon in order to make It trap such a defect which might have been taken place for the very new enactment of the Rules and as I have told it earlier that after 11 days of the enactment of the Rules, the occurrence of this ease was taken place, so the defect in obtaining the permission from the authority by Benzir Ahmed (PWl) who led the trap party is curable under section 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.</u>

53. Now, another important pe1int was raised by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the accused was not given any chance to place his grievance before the commission at the time of enquiry and investigation following the Rules 8 and 11 of the Bidhlmala, In fact, the Rules 8 and 11 are almost similar in their applicability, Rules 8 and 11 of the Bidhlmala are reproduced here for the better understanding of all.

54. The Rule 8 of the Bldhimala runs as follows:

৮। (১) দুর্নীতি বিষয়ক কোন অভিযোগের অনুসন্ধান চলাকালে কমিশন বা কমিশন কর্তৃক ক্ষমতাপ্রাপ্ত কোন কমিশনার বা কর্মকর্তা যদি মনে করে যে, অভিযোগের সহিত সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তির বক্তব্য শ্রবণ করা প্রয়োজন তাহা হইলে অভিযুক্ত ব্যক্তিকে লিখিত নোটিশ প্রদান করিয়া নোটিশে উল্লিখিত সময়সীমার মধ্যে মৌখিক বা লিখিত বক্তব্য পেশ করিবার সুযোগ প্রদান করিতে পারিবে।

(২) উপ-বিধি (১) এর অধীন নোটিশপ্রাপ্ত ব্যক্তি তাহার বিরুদ্ধে আনীত অভিযোগ খন্ডন করিয়া নোটিশে নির্দেশিত সময়সীমার মধ্যে ব্যক্তিগতভাবে বা তাহার নিয়োজিত আইনজীবিসহ মৌখিক বা লিখিত বক্তব্য পেশ করিতে পারিবে এবং উক্তরুপে বক্তব্য পেশ করা হইলে সংশ্লিষ্ট কমিশনার বা কর্মকর্তা উহা সংশ্লিষ্ট নথিতে অন্তর্ভুক্ত করিবেন।

55. While the Rule II of the Bidhlmala runs as follows:

১১। (১) দুর্নীতি বিষয়ক কোন অভিযোগের অনুসন্ধান শেষ হওয়ার পর অভিযোগ প্রাথমিভাবে প্রতিষ্ঠিত হইলে তদন্ত চলাকালে কমিশন যদি মনে করে যে, অভিযোগের সহিত সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তির বক্তব্য শ্রবণ করা প্রয়োজন তাহা হইলে অভিযুক্ত ব্যক্তিকে লিখিত নোটিশ প্রদান করিয়া নোটিশে উল্লিখিত সময়সীমর মধ্যে মৌখিক বা লিখিত বক্তব্য পেশ করিবার সুযোগ প্রদান করিতে পারিবে।

(২) উপ-বিধি (১) এর অধীন নোটিশপ্রাপ্ত ব্যক্তি তাহার বিরুদ্ধে আনীত অভিযোগ খন্ডন করিয়া নোটিশে নির্দেশিত সময় সীমার মধ্যে ব্যক্তিগতভাবে বা তাহার নিয়োজিত আইনজীবিসহ মৌখিক বা লিখিত বক্তব্য পেশ করিতে পারিবে এবং উক্তরুপে বক্তব্য পেশ করা হইলে সংশ্লিষ্ট কমিশনার বা কর্মকর্তা উহা সংশ্লিষ্ট নথিতে অন্তর্ভুক্ত করিবেন।

<u>56. From the Rule 8 of the Bidhimala it appears that in an inquiry against a person on an allegation of corruption, the commission or any other person on his behalf may ask the person to explain his position. Inquiry is generally taken place before the filing of the case. In the instant case though before the lodging of the FIR by PW 1 there was recovery of alleged bribe money from the accused but there was no scope for the PW 1 to prolong the said situation without filing of the case and handing over the accused to the Police Station. So, the very nature of the case did not permit and justify to notify the accused in black and white to explain his position before the lodging of the FIR.</u>

<u>57. From the Rule 11 of the Bidhimala it appears that there are provisions of giving chance to the accused to explain his position at the investigation stage if the Commission thinks it fit and necessary. The underlining portion of the Rule 11 indicates that it is the option of the commission whether they will exercise it or not in the appropriate case.</u>

<u>58. Thus it reveals that it is the total discretion of the Anti-Corruption Commission whether they think it fit and necessary that any accused should be given a chance to explain his position and only then the accused can be afforded with the said opportunity to explain his position before the commission during the investigation. Undoubtedly the provisions of Rule 11 of the Bidhimala affording an opportunity to the accused to place his case before the commission at the time of investigation is very much progressive and dynamic as there may be some special defence or information in favour of the accused which can only be unveiled by the accused but the Rule itself did not confer any right to the accused to explain his position before the Commission or Commissioner and it is the commission who will exercise this option considering the nature of the case. I do not feel that the commission was restrained capriciously from exercising this option. So, I find it difficult to hold that the submitting of charge sheet against the accused without giving him chance to explain his position before the Commission was illegal.</u>

59. As I have told it earlier that the fate of the case as well as of this appeal will be decided ascertaining whether Abdus Salam Khokon gave Taka 4,000 to the accused as part payment of the rents of their ancestral property or as bribe for mutating his name for 0.03 acres of land. A mutation case is always started by filing of a petition for the same. The defence challenging the PW 3 Abdus Salam Khokon suggested to him that he did not file any petition for mutation and the answer of PW 3 on the said suggestion appears to be in the following ways:

60. The file of the mutation case being No. 6154/06-07 has been seized by the Investigating Officer in this case and the said file has been marked as Exhibit-XI. In the said file there appears computer composed petition for mutation comprising the name and figure of Abdus Salam Khokon, In this proceeding there is two admitted signatures of Atdus Salam Khokon, one is in the petition dated 1-4-2007 filed before the PW 1 to lead the trap party and also in the evidence sheet recorded by the trial Court. The signature appears in the petition for mutation did not tally with the admitted signa1Ures of Abdus Salam Khokon made in those two documents that is in the evidence sheet andffi the petition filed before the PW 1.

61. Moreso, the pattern of writing of the signature of Abdus Salam Khokon in the petition for mutation has similarity with the writings of first order on 6-2-2097 in the file of the mutation case. It expressly manifest, that the accused had manuscripted the petition in the name of Abdus Salam Khokon for mutating his name and started the file (Exhibit No. XI) in his own initiative.

62. Over and  above, a notice was served upon the 2nd party and in the said notice, the same type of hand writing is found and by these facts it reveal to me that the evidence of PW 3. Abdus Salam Khokon that "আসামী সব করিয়া লইবে বলিয়াছে" happens to be a fact that when Abdus Salam Khokon had desired for mutating his name the accused did all the acts even the filing of the petition which was required to be filed by Abdus Salam Khokon himself.

63. PW 3 in his cross-examination at one stage stated in the following manner:

"...........আসামী ঐ দিন আমাকে mutation পর্চা DCR খাজনা রশিদ একসাথে দিয়াছেন........................। আমি টাকা দেওয়ার পরই ঘটনার তারিখ আসামী কাগজ ৩টি আমার হাতে দেন।"

64. PW 3 though testified that the accused had handed overthe mutation parcha, the DCR and the rent receipt on the date of occurrence (onl0-4-2007) out the materials on record, particularly the file of the mutation case (Exhibit No. XI) shows that the mutation parch a and the DCR for taka 28 were prepared on 6-3-2007 and 29-3-2007 respectively in the name of Abdus Salam Khokon.

65. The prosecution did not seize those papers from Abdus Salam Khokon but the rent receipts book itself has been seized in this case. The said rent receipt bearing serial No. 714652 within this book has been marked as exhibit X(i) which shows that Taka 2 was received from Abdus Salam Khokon through the said rent receipt on 10-4-2007.

66. PW 12 the Investigating Officer of this case at one stage of his examination-in-chief stated in the following ways:

"তদন্তকারী ৪,০০০ টাকা আবার স্বাক্ষর করে গ্রহন করে, আসামীকে দেবার জন্য নিয়ে গেলে টাকাটা আসামীকে দেবার পরে ২ টাকা মূল্যের একটি খাজনার রশিদ দেয় (নং৭২৪৬৫২) তাং ১০-৪-২০০৭।"

67. In this proceeding the total defence case has been surrounded on a story that since the accused declined to mutate the entire property of plot No. 1664 in the name of Abdus Salam Khokon, he being annoyed of the said fact created this false case playing a drama of handing over Taka 4,000 as part payment ofthe rents of the said land.

68. It is fact that the land of plot No. 1664 is the joint property of Abdus Salam Khokon and his cousin Amirul Islam (PW13) and it is fact that both of them were paying rents separately. On 17- 7-2007 PW 13 Md Amirul Islam paid rents of Taka 3,566 (Exhibit XIII) while on 25-7-2007 Abdus Salam Khokon paid Taka 3,566 (Exhibit XIII (1 ). Thus though there appears some reality that the land of plot No. 1664 are the joint property of Abdus Salam Khokon and their cousin Md Amirul Islam but by simple mutating of the name, the ownership of the land cannot be created. So, the very approach by Abdus Salam Khokon for mutating his or their name in the land of plot No. 1664 cannot be taken as a reliable and probable fact.

69. It is also fact that it is in the evidence of PW 6 Md Sirajul Haque in whose presence themoney was recovered that at the time of nabbing of the accused he told it that Abdus Salam Khokon gave the money as part payment of the rents. The same evidence has been given by the PW 7 Md Anisur Rahman in whose presence the money was seized from the accused. He told that the accused at the time of recovery of money from him told that he had taken the money as part payment of the rents. PW 11 Mr Karnruzzaman, Assistant Commissioner, Narayanganj in whose presence the money was seized from the accused also stated that Mohsin told that he did not take the money as bribe but as rents.

70. The learned Advocate for the appellant putting much emphasis on the above evidence of PWs 6,7 and 11 tried to establish that by the above noted evidence it has been proved that the accused had taken Taka 4,000 not.as bribe but as part payment of the rents. Apparently, this argument appears to be very much appetizing and lucid because at the very initial stage of the case the accused tried to make out a very strong defence case that he took the money not as bribe but as part payment of the rents given by Abdus Salam Khokon. Now, if I compare all these evidence of PWs 6, 7 and 11 side by side with the rent receipt dated 10-4-2007 [Exhibit No. X(i)] it unfurls strongly that accused Mohsin as part performance of his contract with PW 3 Abdus Salam Khokon took Taka 4,000 as bribe issuing and handing over a rent receipt for mutating his name in the 0.03 acres of land. Issuance of the rent receipt by the accused on 10-4-2007 in favour of Abdus Salam Khokon has vanished and brushed aside the all defence plea that Abdus Salam Khokon had gone to Kashipur land office to pay the rents of the joint property.

71. The very strong defence plea in this case that Abdus Salam Khokon had gone at Kashipur Union Land Office on that very date in order to hand over the money as part payment of the rents do not stand at all and this argument did not find any place when it is found that accused Mohsin issued a rent receipt for the mutating of lands in favour of Abdus Salam Khokon, as such I am of the firm view that the said rent receipt [Exhibit No. X(i)] had connected the accused with the occurrence of taking bribe as projected by the prosecution as well as by PW 3 Abdus Salam Khokon.

72. The common proverb of this sub-continent is that a criminal committing criminal offence consciously or unconsciously leaves behind the mark or evidence of the offence that ultimately reflects the persons involvement or indulgement with the occurrence which is fully applicable in this case, because the accused issuing the rent receipt on 10-4-2007 in favour of Abdus Salam Khokon himself proved his involvement with the occurrence ofthe case and had there been no such issuance of rent receipt by this appellant, the prosecution would be in a trouble to prove the involvement of this appellant with the occurrence of this case.

73. PW 3 Abdus Salam Khokon is a neighbour of Kashipur Union Land Office and there is also suggestion that he had created this case in order to harass the accused but I find it difficult to materialize and to conceive this argument because there appears no affairs or any fact for which Abdus Salam Khokon will be so sensitive and interested to cause so harm to the accused planting a case involving the officers of DUDAC and RAB.

74. The defence case appears to have no legal substance and footings when it is found that on the very date of the occurrence a rent receipt [Exhibit No. X(i)] was issued in the name of Abdus Salam Khokon by the accused. So the very presence of Abdus Salam Khokon in the office of the accused justifiably establishes the transaction of money in connection of his mutation case that is why he got the receipt for the same. There is no case in the hands of the defence that the said rent receipt of Taka 2 was not issued on that very day or it has been manifested by any other person. So, I have no hesitation to say that the prosecution case of giving bribe to the accused has been proved beyond all reasonable doubt.

75. The issuance of the rent receipt on 10-4-2007 in favour of Abdus Salam Khokon cannot be disregarded or disbelieved because that is very much' available in the rent receipts book [Exhibit No. X(i)] and which is before me and available with the record. So, the defence version that Abdus Salam Khokon had gone in the land office in order to transact a portion of money of the rents of their joint property and by the said transaction he has created a pantomime cannot be taken as a fact. So, I find that the charge as framed under section 161 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 for taking bribe from Abdus Salam Khokon has been proved. I find that on the proper assessment of the evidence and other materials on record the trial Court found him guilty under the above sections of law.

76. In the result, the appeal is dismissed. The judgment and the order of conviction and sentence dated 4-3-2010 passed by the Special Judge, Court No.4, Dhaka in Special Case No.2 of 2009 is hereby affirmed and upheld. The appellant is directed to surrender in the trial Court within 2 (two) calendar months from the date of receipt of this judgment by the trial Court. If the custody of the appellant from the date of his arrest on 10-4-2007 is more than that of the period of the sentence imposed by the trial Court, he did not require to suffer any sentence more.

Let a copy of this judgment and order along with the lower Court's record be sent to the concerned Court for information and necessary action.

End.
